item.title: llama.cpp GGUF parser CVEs get third-party review
item.description: Penligent published a review of three llama.cpp GGUF parser vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-126974, CVE-2026-126975, CVE-2026-126976), urging teams to verify which upstream parser fixes their GGUF-loading builds actually contain. In the same window, Microsoft's .NET team published a guide on running local llama.cpp models from .NET apps on Windows via the Llama tray app.
item.content:encoded:
Penligent published a review of three llama.cpp GGUF parser vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-126974, CVE-2026-126975, CVE-2026-126976), urging teams to verify which upstream parser fixes their GGUF-loading builds actually contain. In the same window, Microsoft's .NET team published a guide on running local llama.cpp models from .NET apps on Windows via the Llama tray app.

Fixes and other​

  • 2026-11-18: Penligent's Hacking Labs published a security analysis of three llama.cpp GGUF parser CVEs whose Zero Day Initiative advisories (ZDI-26-954, ZDI-26-975, ZDI-26-976) were released Nov 13, 2026. The review covers an integer overflow in GGUF parsing, inadequate length validation before a heap-buffer copy (both linking upstream PR 31336), and an integer overflow when parsing audio multimodal projector GGUF data (a separate commit), and notes the November 18 feed appearance is not a new disclosure date. The practical takeaway: establish which parser fixes, including optional multimodal and control-vector paths, exist in the binary that loads your model files. Source: https://www.penligent.ai/hackinglabs/cve-2026-126974/

Community​

  • Late November 2026 (published 2026-11-23 per the post): Microsoft's .NET team published a guide showing how to run local LLMs in .NET apps on Windows using llama.cpp, built around the Llama on Windows tray app from the Hugging Face and llama.cpp teams, with a sample repo calling a llama.cpp server from a .NET 11 C# file-based app. Source: https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/local-models-dotnet-llama-windows/

Sources​

  • https://www.penligent.ai/hackinglabs/cve-2026-126974/
  • https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/local-models-dotnet-llama-windows/

item.title: n8n 2.49.0 and 2.50.0 ship, CVE-2026-119408 gets a deep dive
item.description: n8n shipped two stable releases this window: 2.49.0 (Nov 17), a broad update centered on AI agents with webhook channels, approval support, agent management, and tool guardrails, and 2.50.0 (Nov 24), which fixed AI Agent chat-memory handling, n8n Assistant behavior, and Public API import/export. Also, TryHackMe detailed CVE-2026-119408, a high-severity code-execution flaw patched in 2.42.6, and Activepieces published a detailed analysis of Nod, n8n's local personal agent.
item.content:encoded:
n8n shipped two stable releases this window: 2.49.0 (Nov 17), a broad update centered on AI agents with webhook channels, approval support, agent management, and tool guardrails, and 2.50.0 (Nov 24), which fixed AI Agent chat-memory handling, n8n Assistant behavior, and Public API import/export. Also, TryHackMe detailed CVE-2026-119408, a high-severity code-execution flaw patched in 2.42.6, and Activepieces published a detailed analysis of Nod, n8n's local personal agent.

Releases​

  • 2.49.0 (Nov 17, 2026): broad update focused on AI agents, adding webhook channels, approval support, agent management, skills editing, and tool guardrails; also expands API and OAuth capabilities and fixes numerous reliability, workflow, and editor issues (Releasebot).
  • 2.50.0 (Nov 24, 2026): stable release with bug fixes including AI Agent chat-memory handling (drops turns with empty content), n8n Assistant improvements, Public API behavior for workflow package import/export, and fixes across AWS Bedrock, Baserow, and HTTP Request nodes (n8n CHANGELOG).

Fixes and other​

  • TryHackMe (Nov 23, 2026) detailed CVE-2026-119408 (CVSS 8.7, High): a user with workflow permissions can run JavaScript in the main application process via the deprecated Function, Function Item, and LangChain Code nodes, outside task-runner isolation, which can expose the instance encryption key. The vendor patch shipped in 2.42.6, and the write-up links a hands-on training room (TryHackMe).

Community​

  • Activepieces (Nov 21, 2026) published a detailed analysis of Nod, n8n's local personal agent released as a research preview that can connect to n8n to build, test, and run workflows. As of 2026-11-11, n8n had not published a launch date or source code, and no native third-party integration exists yet (Activepieces).

Sources​

  • https://releasebot.io/updates/n8n
  • https://raw.githubusercontent.com/n8n-io/n8n/master/CHANGELOG.md
  • https://tryhackme.com/resources/blog/how-deprecated-n8n-nodes-put-workflow-credentials-at-risk
  • https://www.activepieces.com/blog/nod-by-n8n-what-it-is-and-whats-known-2026

item.title: LlamaCPP v1.0.0: llama.cpp and ggml hit their first stable release
item.description: llama.cpp and ggml have reached their first stable v1.0.0 releases on November 13, 2026, ending roughly three and a half years of sub-1.0 development. The team, which has been developing the project at Hugging Face since February 2026, committed to semantic versioning going forward: major version bumps will only occur for breaking API or ABI changes.
item.content:encoded:
llama.cpp and ggml have reached their first stable v1.0.0 releases on November 13, 2026, ending roughly three and a half years of sub-1.0 development. The team, which has been developing the project at Hugging Face since February 2026, committed to semantic versioning going forward: major version bumps will only occur for breaking API or ABI changes.

Releases​

  • llama.cpp v1.0.0 and ggml v1.0.0 (November 13, 2026): ggml-org published the first stable 1.0.0 of llama.cpp (libllama) and its underlying ggml library. This marks the first 1.0.0 milestone for the project, which started in March 2023 as an inference engine for Meta's LLaMA model and now supports most open-source LLMs on a wide range of hardware. Future major version updates will be tied to compatibility-breaking API/ABI changes. Source: Hugging Face blog, llama.cpp v1.0.0: A stronger foundation for the local AI ecosystem

Community​

  • Milestone covered by GIGAZINE (November 16, 2026): GIGAZINE reported that llama.cpp and ggml have finally reached version 1.0.0. The article traces the project's history from its March 2023 release by Georgi Gerganov, through its 2026 move to Hugging Face, and notes its role as the underlying engine for popular local AI applications such as LM Studio and Unsloth Desktop. Source: GIGAZINE, 'llama.cpp' has finally reached version 1.0.0

Sources​

  • https://huggingface.co/blog/ggml-org/llama-cpp-v1
  • https://gigazine.net/gsc_news/en/20261116-llama-cpp-ggml-milestone/

item.title: Omarchy 4.5.1 point release takes shape as next version adds Omaview and new default apps
item.description: Since the Omarchy 4.5 release, maintainer activity has been split between the first point release, 4.5.1, and a busy stretch of feature merges on the next version. Ryan Hughes merged a PR backporting 46 bug fixes toward 4.5.1, while DHH merged several headline features including Omaview, two new default games, and Fantasi as a default app.
item.content:encoded:
Since the Omarchy 4.5 release, maintainer activity has been split between the first point release, 4.5.1, and a busy stretch of feature merges on the next version. Ryan Hughes merged a PR backporting 46 bug fixes toward 4.5.1, while DHH merged several headline features including Omaview, two new default games, and Fantasi as a default app.

Releases​

  • Omarchy 4.5.1 point release takes shape: on November 17, maintainer Ryan Hughes merged a pull request backporting 46 bug fixes toward the first point release of Omarchy 4.5 (https://omarchycentral.com/section/releases/).

Features​

  • Omaview replaces imv and mpv: DHH merged a pull request on November 15 replacing the separate imv image viewer and mpv player with Omaview, Omarchy's own unified media viewer, for the next version (https://omarchycentral.com/section/releases/).
  • Two new default games: DHH merged two pull requests on November 16 adding Cards (Klondike solitaire) and Checkmate (3D chess) as default apps (https://omarchycentral.com/section/releases/).
  • Fantasi becomes a default app: DHH merged a pull request into the quattro branch on November 18 making Fantasi, Omarchy's local image maker, a default app (https://omarchycentral.com/section/releases/).
  • First-boot setup expands: on November 14, first-boot setup was merged to gain the installer's screens, plus OEM branding and an agreement step, for machines prepared by others (https://omarchycentral.com/section/releases/).
  • T3 Code adopts full Omarchy theming: Ryan Hughes merged a pull request on November 18 so T3 Code now follows Omarchy's fonts, chrome, and corner styles, not just its colors (https://omarchycentral.com/section/releases/).

Fixes and other​

  • Slack theme sync removed before shipping: DHH merged pull request #18788 on November 15 to remove live Slack theme sync after Slack 4.53 refused to launch with it, pulling the feature before it reached a release (https://omarchycentral.com/section/releases/).

Sources​

  • https://omarchycentral.com/section/releases/

item.title: Strata 0.2.16 ships its own inference engine
item.description: Strata 0.2.16 landed on 18 November 2026, moving every engine (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel Arc, Apple Silicon, DGX Spark) to Strata's own engine code with no ggml or llama.cpp matrix kernels. The release also reorganizes the repository into engine/, app/, terminal/, docs/ and tools/, and fixes a silent correctness bug on Mac M1-M4 from 0.2.15 plus several Windows and Linux crashes. LinuxCompatible covered the release the next day.
item.content:encoded:
Strata 0.2.16 landed on 18 November 2026, moving every engine (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel Arc, Apple Silicon, DGX Spark) to Strata's own engine code with no ggml or llama.cpp matrix kernels. The release also reorganizes the repository into engine/, app/, terminal/, docs/ and tools/, and fixes a silent correctness bug on Mac M1-M4 from 0.2.15 plus several Windows and Linux crashes. LinuxCompatible covered the release the next day.

Releases​

  • Strata v0.2.16 was released on 18 November 2026 (app and Terminal at 0.2.16, engines and Control at 0.1.62, update feed sequence 128). The repo was reorganized into engine/, app/, terminal/, docs/ and tools/, and existing models, chats and settings carry over on update: https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/releases/tag/v0.2.16

item.title: Coder v2.38.7 becomes latest stable as v2.39 mainline ships
item.description: Coder moved the 2.38 line to the latest stable release with v2.38.7 on November 10, 2026, carrying a breaking change that validates workspace app URLs on the server. The v2.39 mainline line advanced in the same window: v2.39.0 shipped on November 3 with breaking changes, and v2.39.1 followed on November 10 as a patch release.
item.content:encoded:
Coder moved the 2.38 line to the latest stable release with v2.38.7 on November 10, 2026, carrying a breaking change that validates workspace app URLs on the server. The v2.39 mainline line advanced in the same window: v2.39.0 shipped on November 3 with breaking changes, and v2.39.1 followed on November 10 as a patch release.

Releases​

  • v2.38.7 (Nov 10, 2026): now the latest stable release ("Stable since November 10, 2026"). Breaking change: validate workspace app URLs on the server (#31262). Also fixes: ignore retired OAuth2 scopes such as task:* (#31117) and tighten up database connection errors (#31850). Source: https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.38.7
  • v2.39.0 (Nov 3, 2026): November mainline release. Includes breaking changes, such as the connection log migration that blocks reads and writes during the rewrite of the connection_logs table (#30466). Coder advises enterprise users without a staging environment to stay on the latest stable release while 2.39 is refined. Source: https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.39.0
  • v2.39.1 (Nov 10, 2026): mainline patch release on the 2.39 line, fixing tightened-up database connection errors (#31850) and backporting release calendar and install version documentation refresh for v2.39.0 (#31716). Source: https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.39.1

Fixes and other​

  • Server-side validation of workspace app URLs lands in v2.38.7 as a breaking fix, so misconfigured workspace app URLs are now rejected by the server (https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.38.7).
  • Database connection error handling was tightened on both the 2.38 and 2.39 lines via #31850 (https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.39.1).

Sources​

  • https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.38.7
  • https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.39.0

item.title: LlamaCPP 0.9.0 lands OCP FP8 and a local speech stack
item.description: llama.cpp v0.9.0 shipped on 4 November 2026, adding OCP FP8 E4M3 quantization, a flashattnext_rows op that makes the unified KV cache efficient for multi-sequence inference, and a generic batched tensor copy API. The release expands the audio stack with Chatterbox TTS, Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and predefined Pocket TTS voices, adds four new architectures (Clover, Limite, Metis-1.6, Mistral Large 4), and bumps ggml to 0.29.0 with early NCCL multi-node tensor parallel. Community coverage on dev.to explored the new local speech stack and its limits on Windows.
item.content:encoded:
llama.cpp v0.9.0 shipped on 4 November 2026, adding OCP FP8 E4M3 quantization, a flash_attn_ext_rows op that makes the unified KV cache efficient for multi-sequence inference, and a generic batched tensor copy API. The release expands the audio stack with Chatterbox TTS, Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and predefined Pocket TTS voices, adds four new architectures (Clover, Limite, Metis-1.6, Mistral Large 4), and bumps ggml to 0.29.0 with early NCCL multi-node tensor parallel. Community coverage on dev.to explored the new local speech stack and its limits on Windows.

Releases​

  • v0.9.0 was released on 2026-11-04 as the latest stable version of llama.cpp. It adds OCP FP8 E4M3 quantization support, the new flash_attn_ext_rows op, a batched tensor copy API, and major prefill optimizations for Gemma 4 E2B/E4B models. (source)
  • v0.9.0 updates ggml to v0.29.0, bringing early NCCL multi-node tensor parallel support. (source)

Features​

  • v0.9.0 adds first-class Chatterbox TTS, Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe and predefined Pocket TTS voices, extending audio generation and transcription in the toolchain. (source)
  • v0.9.0 adds four new model architectures: Clover, Limite, Metis-1.6 and Mistral Large 4. (source)
  • Nightly build b12191 (2026-11-07) introduces a --moe-cache-cpu-share parameter that lets a fraction of Mixture-of-Experts cache misses be computed on the host CPU instead of the primary device, plus a new moe-cache-tune.py script to profile and recommend --moe-cache-mib and CPU share settings. (source)

Community​

  • A dev.to article posted on 2026-11-05 details how v0.9.0's llama-tts tool and multimodal server support make Chatterbox TTS and Nemotron Transcribe usable as a fully local speech stack, and notes that Windows capture-path latency still limits real-time audio. (source)

Sources​

  • https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tag/v0.9.0
  • https://dev.to/madnessbrains_i/llamacpp-090-ships-chatterbox-tts-and-ocp-fp8-local-speech-still-dies-on-the-windows-capture-10n0
  • https://aiunderstanding.org/news/llama-cpp-introduces-cpu-offloading-for-mixture-of-experts-cache-misses

item.title: Ninfer4090 perplexity tool learns the fork KV dtypes
item.description: Ninfer4090's perplexity evaluator gained support for the fork's KV dtypes on 2026-10-24, finally allowing perplexity to be measured for the production 4-bit KV mode. The same day brought a small frontend validation fix and a community triage round recorded in the project ledger.
item.content:encoded:
Ninfer4090's perplexity evaluator gained support for the fork's KV dtypes on 2026-10-24, finally allowing perplexity to be measured for the production 4-bit KV mode. The same day brought a small frontend validation fix and a community triage round recorded in the project ledger.

Features​

  • ninfer-perplexity now accepts rk8v4, rk4v4, rk4v4-e8 and rk2v4-e8 KV dtypes (parser hunk from T-Crypt's PR #16). Previously it only parsed bf16, int8, fp8, nvfp4 and k8v4, so the production KV mode (rk4v4-e8) had no perplexity number. First used in the 2026-10-24 triage baseline on the v2 artifact: A16 4.363573 vs INT8 4.358936 on the quick corpus. Source: https://github.com/sergiuszm/ninfer-4090/commit/f3f4579ccd45139329fc40a8d7362d817f05d059

Fixes and other​

item.title: Omarchy 4.5 lands with desktop mode and Apple Silicon support
item.description: Omarchy 4.5 (codenamed Quattro RS) shipped on November 5, 2026 as the project's first big feature release since Quattro, after more than 740 pull requests from 180+ contributors in twelve weeks. The headline changes: a traditional desktop mode alongside the tiling default, native installation on Apple Silicon MacBooks (M1/M2/M3/Neo), and interface support for 50 languages. The project also expanded beyond x86_64 for the first time, with reported support for NVIDIA N1X laptops and DGX Spark, while Snapdragon X laptop support is forthcoming.
item.content:encoded:
Omarchy 4.5 (codenamed Quattro RS) shipped on November 5, 2026 as the project's first big feature release since Quattro, after more than 740 pull requests from 180+ contributors in twelve weeks. The headline changes: a traditional desktop mode alongside the tiling default, native installation on Apple Silicon MacBooks (M1/M2/M3/Neo), and interface support for 50 languages. The project also expanded beyond x86_64 for the first time, with reported support for NVIDIA N1X laptops and DGX Spark, while Snapdragon X laptop support is forthcoming.

Releases​

  • Omarchy v4.5.0 (Quattro RS) was released to GitHub on November 5, 2026: the first major feature release since Quattro, adding a traditional desktop mode next to the tiling default, a native installer for M1/M2/M3/Neo MacBooks, and 50 languages (source).
  • The release was announced on the project's news page on November 4, 2026, with instructions for existing users (Update > Omarchy) and a direct download for new machines (source).

Features​

  • Floating workspaces with a dock: Super + L cycles any workspace between tiling, scrolling, and floating; floating windows get themed titlebars, a dock of pinned and running apps, and Super + M minimizes to the dock (source).
  • Native Apple Silicon support: the Omarchy M team shipped a native Mac installer for M1/M2/M3/Neo MacBooks, building on Asahi Linux work (source).
  • First multi-architecture release: beyond x86_64, Phoronix reports support for Apple Silicon hardware, NVIDIA N1X laptops, and DGX Spark desktops, with Snapdragon X support planned (source).
  • More desktop customizations, including per-monitor workspaces, rebuilt notifications, an Appearance menu, and four new default apps (Hype, Monologue, Signed, Disktree), plus 50 languages (source).

Community​

  • Phoronix covered the release on November 5, 2026, highlighting the distro's expansion beyond x86_64 and its new desktop customization options (source).

Sources​

  • https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/releases/tag/v4.5.0
  • https://omarchy.org/news/2026/11/omarchy-4-5/
  • https://www.phoronix.com/news/Omarchy-4.5-Released

item.title: Omarchy Core grows: Alcantara and Skyum join, Greptile becomes Distinguished Corporate Patron
item.description: Omarchy announced major growth on its people side this month. Marcelo Alcantara and Birk Skyum, credited as two of the people doing the most to take Omarchy beyond x86, joined Omarchy Core on November 5. The Omacom Foundation also added Greptile as a Distinguished Corporate Patron (October 15) and hired HANCORE as Head of Design and Community (October 27).
item.content:encoded:
Omarchy announced major growth on its people side this month. Marcelo Alcantara and Birk Skyum, credited as two of the people doing the most to take Omarchy beyond x86, joined Omarchy Core on November 5. The Omacom Foundation also added Greptile as a Distinguished Corporate Patron (October 15) and hired HANCORE as Head of Design and Community (October 27).

Community​

  • On November 5, 2026, Omarchy announced that Marcelo Alcantara and Birk Skyum are joining Omarchy Core. Alcantara coordinated the Omarchy M effort, a sixteen-person team that shipped the native macOS installer in Omarchy 4.5, letting Omarchy run alongside macOS on Apple Silicon Macs; Skyum's work on Omarchy Dragon is also highlighted in the post. Source: https://omarchy.org/news/2026/11/marcelo-alcantara-and-birk-skyum-join-omarchy-core/
  • On October 15, 2026, the Omacom Foundation announced Greptile as a Distinguished Corporate Patron, contributing $150,000 in tokens for its PR review service so every pull request coming into Omarchy can be reviewed. The post notes Greptile has already reviewed almost 1,500 pull requests, and that across the 60 most recently merged PRs it reviewed, it flagged 39 issues it rated as serious, including a Turkish-locale lowercasing bug in laptop model matching. Source: https://omarchy.org/news/2026/10/greptile-joins-as-a-distinguished-corporate-patron/
  • On October 27, 2026, the Omacom Foundation announced it is hiring HANCORE as Head of Design and Community, making him its fourth staff member alongside Krzysztof on Kernel, outfoxxed on Shell, and Emir on Infrastructure. He moves from his Omarchy AIR residency seat, where he started the plugin marketplace that grew into the official plugin catalogue with six thousand plugins, and whose themes (Solitude and Last Horizon) ship with Omarchy. Source: https://omarchy.org/news/2026/10/omacom-foundation-hires-hancore/

item.description: Strata 0.2.13 (engine 0.1.59) shipped on November 9, 2026 with new per-card DFlash2 drafting defaults, a much faster app start, an Intel Arc determinism fix, a Linux expert-store loading fix, and groundwork for Qwen4. Press coverage highlights the Strix Halo Terminal launch fix, which cut startup from up to about 10 minutes to 60-85 seconds, and notes the project has passed 42,000 GitHub stars.
item.content:encoded:
Strata 0.2.13 (engine 0.1.59) shipped on November 9, 2026 with new per-card DFlash2 drafting defaults, a much faster app start, an Intel Arc determinism fix, a Linux expert-store loading fix, and groundwork for Qwen4. Press coverage highlights the Strix Halo Terminal launch fix, which cut startup from up to about 10 minutes to 60-85 seconds, and notes the project has passed 42,000 GitHub stars.

Releases​

  • Strata 0.2.13 released on 2026-11-09 (app and Terminal 0.2.13, Control and all engine packages 0.1.59; DGX Spark also receives 0.2.13). The update brings new card-specific DFlash2 drafting defaults (49.1 tok/s on Strix Halo, +5.2%), a faster app start, and Qwen4 groundwork: release notes.

Fixes and other​

  • The release includes a Strix Halo Terminal launch fix reducing startup from up to ~594 s to 60-85 s, an Intel Arc determinism fix, and a fix for broken Linux expert-store loading, plus follow-up 0.2.13.1 letting the Linux desktop app set up models on Intel Arc cards: release notes.

Community​

  • Linux Compatible covered the 0.2.13 release on 2026-11-09, calling it the most practical update yet to the engine and noting Strata has climbed past 42,000 GitHub stars: article.

item.title: n8n 2.43.7 stable lands execution suspension as ZoomInfo ships native node
item.description: n8n shipped four releases between Oct 14 and Oct 16, led by stable 2.43.7, which can now suspend in-flight production executions when a worker shuts down. The biggest ecosystem news came from ZoomInfo, which launched a verified native n8n node exposing its GTM Context Graph for workflows and AI agents.
item.content:encoded:
n8n shipped four releases between Oct 14 and Oct 16, led by stable 2.43.7, which can now suspend in-flight production executions when a worker shuts down. The biggest ecosystem news came from ZoomInfo, which launched a verified native n8n node exposing its GTM Context Graph for workflows and AI agents.

Releases​

  • 2026-10-16: n8n 2.43.7 (latest stable) released, adding the ability to suspend in-flight production executions at worker shutdown in core. Release
  • 2026-10-15: n8n 2.43.6 released with a core fix creating a fresh XML parser for each webhook request body. Release
  • 2026-10-14: n8n 2.43.5 released, showing Gemini models by name and listing prioritized models first in model pickers. Release
  • 2026-10-14: n8n 1.123.85, a routine maintenance release for the legacy 1.x branch with no notable changes listed. Release

Features​

  • 2026-10-12: ZoomInfo announced a native, verified ZoomInfo node inside n8n, built and maintained by ZoomInfo. Once a workflow authenticates with a customer's own ZoomInfo credentials, it can search contacts and companies, enrich records, and monitor buying-signal and intent data from ZoomInfo's GTM Context Graph via GTM.AI. Announcement

Fixes and other​

  • 2026-10-15: Webhook XML parsing fixed in 2.43.6 by creating a fresh XML parser for each request body. Release
  • 2026-10-14: chunk() expression extension now validates its size argument, shipped in 2.43.5. Release
